entries.definition: openly distrustful and unwilling to confide
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainer twin of *distrustful*, and a shade more tentative.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the telling rather than the feeling - pride said out loud too often.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Literal soot in this sense, and one of a great many senses this word carries.
examples: with feet black from playing outdoors
his shirt was black within an hour

entries.definition: with smiles; in a smiling manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *smiling*: describes the evidence rather than the mood, which is why it can be worn falsely.
examples: the girl reminded her smilingly of their childhood spent together

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *naive*: the everyday word, and gentler than it looks - it blames inexperience, not intellect.
examples: he believed, naively, that she would leave him her money

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *uncivil*: formal and slightly distant - the complaint of someone invoking a standard.
examples: he treats his former wife uncivilly

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pictures the act, and the smallness of the coin does the condemning.
examples: a penny-pinching miserly old man

entries.definition: deprived of life; no longer living
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical and detached: it names the absence of life rather than mourning it.
examples: a lifeless body

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The complaint as noise: continuous, and no longer being listened to.

entries.definition: characterized by quickness and ease in learning
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Common approval of quickness; in some uses it edges toward cunning.
examples: smart children talk earlier than the average

entries.definition: with eagerness; in an eager manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *eager*: warm and forward-looking; the desire is presented as a credit to the person.
examples: the news was eagerly awaited

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *gorgeous*: dazzling and enthusiastic - beauty that stops you.
examples: the Princess was gorgeously dressed

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *complacent*: contentment that should have been alarm - the danger was there to be seen.
examples: he complacently lived out his life as a village school teacher

entries.definition: not pretended; sincerely felt or expressed
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Defined against pretence, which is a curious way to have to say it.
examples: her interest in people was unfeigned

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The formal word for a short fuse, and the most neutral in tone.

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Grand phrasing for an ordinary end, which is why it turns comic.

entries.definition: appropriate (as property entrusted to one's care) fraudulently to one's own use
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The bloodless official term - what an auditor writes instead of 'stole'.

entries.definition: in a corrupt and deceitful manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *deceitful*: puts the intent in view: not merely wrong, but meaning to mislead.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Affectation as a whole manner - too studied to be trusted.
examples: an insufferably precious performance

entries.definition: with cynicism; in a cynical manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *cynical*: assumes the worst motive as a general rule, which saves the trouble of looking.
examples: Larsen's frost-blackened lips curved cynically

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Small, weak crying - pitying of an animal or a child, belittling of an adult.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Neat and in good shape - credits effort.
examples: a body kept trim by exercise

entries.definition: lacking refinement or cultivation or taste
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Nearly forgiving: the material is good, the finishing was never done.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain compound, and the one most likely to be said out loud.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The image is a farmyard bird at dawn: loud, repetitive and pleased with itself.

entries.definition: worn and broken down by hard use
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Broken down past repair, and cruel when turned on a person.
examples: a decrepit bus … its seats held together with friction tape

entries.definition: filled or scattered with a disorderly accumulation of objects or rubbish
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The rubbish sense has taken over, and litter is somebody's fault.
examples: the storm left the driveway littered with sticks and debris

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the person a knave; the word has aged into costume drama.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *smug*: the social version: pleasure in being right, worn where others can see it.
examples: the bureaucrats explained smugly that the facts provided by their own experts show no cause for concern

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *selfish*: the plain moral word, and the one that gets used in real arguments.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises ingenuity - though 'too clever' turns it into a fault.
examples: you are a clever man … you reason well and your wit is bold
a clever solution nobody else saw

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral in form, but the turning away is itself the act.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and slightly distant - the complaint of someone invoking a standard.
examples: want nothing from you but to get away from your uncivil tongue

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Playground taunt - mocking rather than grave.

entries.definition: having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal contempt - superiority worn openly, with a raised eyebrow.
examples: his mother eyed my clothes with a supercilious air

entries.definition: stubbornly obstructive and unwilling to cooperate
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and furious - it says the obstruction is the whole point.
examples: unions … have never been as bloody-minded about demarcation as the shipbuilders

entries.definition: (of a female body) healthily plump and vigorous
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm and admiring - full-figured in an attractive way.

entries.definition: lacking refinement or cultivation or taste
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Once simply *unknown*; the strangeness curdled into rudeness.
examples: an untutored and uncouth human being
an uncouth soldier — a real tough guy

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most contemptuous word here; the invented sound does the sneering.

entries.definition: humble in spirit or manner; suggesting retiring mildness or even cowed submissiveness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The virtue the family is named for: an accurate view of oneself, held without fuss.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *grotesque*: distorted to the point of unsettling - beyond plain ugliness.
examples: behind the house lay two nude figures grotesquely bald, with deliberate knife-slashes marking their bodies

entries.definition: make off with belongings of others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sneaky and small-scale, with a faintly comic ring.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises by refusing to entertain doubt - it closes the argument rather than winning it.
examples: an unquestionable antique

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Euphemistic. *Close with money* is what you say when you do not want to say stingy.
examples: very close (or near) with his money

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: This sense is rare and easily missed - a reader will hear the body word first.

entries.definition: full of or characterized by loud and nonmusical sounds
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain complaint, and a mild one - noise is expected in most places.
examples: a noisy cafeteria
a small noisy dog

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *bonny*: scottish and northern English warmth - healthy and pleasing.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: From Gascony, whose people were reputed braggarts - a learned word for a common fault.
